subject: Bootstrapping plan: tenant mapping, imaging, and storage orchestration for HelioGrid
messages:
From: Sasha Nguyen <sasha@heliogrid.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng@heliogrid.com
Date: 2027-06-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem deployment: bootstrapping plan & questions

Hi Laura / Neha,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We sketched a high level expectation for the first HelioGrid site and I promised to drop a short list of questions so we can align the bootstrapping/runbook. Quick context: this is a single-rack site with 8 compute nodes (4x GPU-capable), 3 controller nodes, a pair of 10Gb iSCSI targets for archival, and local NVMe on each compute node for low-latency caches.

Can you help confirm the following so we can schedule the first onsite week?
- Recommended sequence to image and join nodes to the cluster (PXE vs manual BMC); we prefer PXE but need a concrete script.
- Tenant mapping approach: we want 3 initial tenants (platform, canary-app, analytics) with the option to isolate their data on separate PV backends. Is that straightforward?
- Storage layout recommendation: which workloads should use local NVMe vs replicated blockstore vs iSCSI long-term?
- Any constraints on CIDR sizes / BGP / MTU we should provide to our networking team before they wire the rack?

I've attached the site inventory and basic rack diagram (heliogrid-site-inventory.xlsx). Can you also share a short list of preflight checks we can run remotely before the engineer lands?

Thanks,
Sasha Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering
HelioGrid
(attachment: heliogrid-site-inventory.xlsx, 58KB)
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Nguyen <sasha@heliogrid.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-27T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: bootstrapping plan & questions

Sasha — thanks for the clear list. High level answer first, then specific attachments and next steps.

High level plan (short):
- Preflight (remote): inventory check, BMC reachability, OOB IPs, time sync, DNS entries, and thin provisioning of disks.
- Imaging & join: PXE-based golden image (we provide playbook) -> kubeadm join with pre-provisioned kubelet bootstrap tokens -> label node pools during join.
- Tenant mapping: start with three logical namespaces mapped to three storage profiles (local-fast, replicated-block, archival-block). Use RBAC + network policies to isolate traffic.
- Rollout: canary tenant first (1 app pod + 1 replica of model-serving) for 72 hours, then expand to analytics, then platform.

Node pool recommendations (initial):
- control-plane: 3 x m16-large (redundant etcd; dedicated control plane VLAN)
- infra: 2 x m8-standard (monitoring, logging, ingress)
- compute-gpu: 4 x g4.8 (GPU-accelerated tenants)
- cache-local: use local NVMe ephemeral for model KV cache, scheduled with local persistent volumes (LVM CSI).

Storage guidance:
- local-fast (LVM CSI on NVMe): low latency, non-replicated, suitable for KV caches and short-lived checkpoints.
- replicated-block (Ceph RBD or Longhorn): durable, cross-node failover for persistent volumes (DBs, model artifacts). We recommend Ceph RBD for larger sites; Longhorn can work short-term.
- archival (iSCSI -> object gateway): for cold data; set lifecycle retention and move to S3 gateway.

Network / infra items to provide now to your net team:
- Pod network CIDR: 10.64.0.0/13
- Service CIDR: 10.96.0.0/12
- Cluster ASN for BGP: 65050 (we peer at the aggregation switch)
- MTU: 9000 preferred for model payloads (confirm with TOR)

Attachments: runbook-bootstrapping-v1.pdf (boot sequence + checklists), tenant-mapping-template.csv (mapping template you can fill).

Next steps / asks:
1) Sasha: confirm on-site engineer name and whether PXE server will be on-site or we should bring a USB fallback.
2) Neha: can you prepare the Golden image and playbook; we need a checksum for procurement and customs.
3) Karthik: please add technical notes on CSI drivers and failure modes (cc'd).

I'll follow up with a short call to walk the team through the runbook.

— Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Deployments
Redwood Inference
(attachment: runbook-bootstrapping-v1.pdf, 420KB)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sasha Nguyen <sasha@heliogrid.com>
Date: 2027-06-28T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: bootstrapping plan & questions

Thanks — diving into the technical constraints / proposals. Long but intended to be actionable.

Imaging & bootstrapping
- PXE preferred: we'll provide a reproducible PXE + iPXE step that chainloads a minimal initramfs and runs an unattended installer. Fallback: BMC + preseed USB image.
- Token lifetime: create a short-lived kubeadm bootstrap token (TTL 24h) and use external CA signing for kubelet cert rotation in the first week.

Networking & routing
- MTU 9000 across TOR and uplinks; if not possible, we add fragmentation-aware settings and reduce pod MTU to 1400.
- Calico in BGP mode (no IPIP) if your aggregation supports BGP peering; it reduces NAT overhead. Provide L2/L3 diagrams and we will annotate with required peer ranges.
- Node CIDR allocation we recommend /24 per node (for 4K pods scaling headroom) but for this size 10.64.0.0/13 works fine.

Storage specifics
- Local NVMe: present as LVM volumes via local-path-provisioner or LVM-CSI. Use node-level wear monitoring and a scheduled eviction policy: node-local eviction threshold at 80% and pod-level QoS for checkpoints.
- Ceph RBD vs Longhorn: Ceph RBD (with at least 3 OSDs across nodes) gives stable replication and is preferred for database-like volumes. Longhorn is easier to operate for smaller teams but has rebuild storm risk.
- iSCSI archival: present to a pair of targets for HA; ensure multipath and path monitoring. Archive volumes should be mounted read-only in some recovery scenarios.

Failure modes / ops playbook highlights
- Control-plane split-brain: ensure etcd quorum by fencing (BMC power-control) scripts and an automated etcd snapshot replication to S3 gateway.
- Disk failure on compute with local NVMe: operator should drain node, copy checkpoint metadata to replicated-block then replace disk (we provide script).
- Network partition: traffic-policing to limit tokens; automatic fallback to smaller model variants if latency spikes beyond SLA.

CSI & drivers
- LVM-CSI for local NVMe; RBD CSI for Ceph; csi-provisioner versions pinned to avoid compatibility drift. We'll include a version matrix in the repo.

Attachments: pxe-imaging-playbook.md (playbook + ipxe configs).

I'll drop the imaging scripts and a small test harness in the shared Drive. Happy to jump on a tech call.

— Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
(attachment: pxe-imaging-playbook.md, 22KB)

Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: bootstrapping plan & questions

Appreciate the quick turn here. I'll own timeline & sign-off items from Redwood's side to keep things moving. Proposed timeline (target):
- Week 0: paperwork, customs, golden-image checksum signed by Neha (we need checksum for procurement).
- Week 1 (onsite): rack integration, PXE imaging, control-plane formation, basic monitoring up.
- Week 2: deploy canary tenant and run 72h soak; collect perf telemetry.
- Week 3: expand to analytics and platform tenants; handoff to HelioGrid SRE for daily ops.

Action items now:
- Sasha: confirm onsite engineer contact and whether they will open port 623 for BMC.
- Procurement (HelioGrid): start customs paperwork and provide expected arrival date of the gear.
- Neha: provide golden-image SHA256 checksum and a brief note on included packages.
- Karthik: can you provide the CSI version matrix and the pxe image checksum by tomorrow?

If all good I will send a brief one-page kickoff email to the HelioGrid exec sponsor and schedule the first preflight call.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
